title: The Courage to Speak
content:
The first rays of the morning sun slowly spread across the peaceful hills of Shimla.

A cool breeze drifted through the open window of Yashwanth's room.

Yet...

Despite the beauty of the morning...

There was no peace inside his heart.

He stood near the window, staring silently into the distance.

His mind was drowning in questions.

How would his father react?

Would he understand?

Or would everything fall apart the moment the truth came out?

The more he thought about it...

The heavier his heart became.

Just then...

A gentle knock echoed through the room.

Before Yashwanth could respond, Siddu quietly walked inside.

One glance at his friend was enough.

He didn't need to ask what was wrong.

Yashwanth's trembling hands...

His restless eyes...

And the fear written across his face...

Told Siddu everything.

He walked over and gently placed a hand on Yashwanth's shoulder.

"Yash..."

Yashwanth slowly turned around.

The moment he saw Siddu, the fear he had been suppressing overflowed.

"You finally came..."

"I've been thinking about this all night."

"I don't know how to tell my father."

"What if he refuses?"

"What if I lose everything?"

Siddu smiled reassuringly.

"Calm your mind."

He looked straight into Yashwanth's eyes.

"If you don't gather the courage to speak the truth..."

"You'll lose the person you love without even trying."

He paused for a moment.

"He is your father."

"He deserves to know what's in your heart."

"And you deserve the chance to fight for your own happiness."

"There is only one way forward."

"Speak the truth."

Yashwanth closed his eyes.

Taking a deep breath...

He slowly nodded.

"You're right."

"No matter what happens..."

"I'll tell him everything."

A proud smile appeared on Siddu's face.

"That's the Yashwanth I know."

Without wasting another moment, the two friends stepped out of the house and began walking toward Yashwanth's parents' home.

The quiet streets of Shimla welcomed them with a cool morning breeze.

Neither of them spoke much.

Sometimes...

The strongest support doesn't come through words.

It comes from simply knowing someone is walking beside you.

After several minutes...

They were only a short distance away from the house.

Suddenly...

Siddu's phone began to ring.

He glanced at the screen.

His expression immediately turned serious.

"Excuse me for a minute."

He stepped aside and answered the call.

Yashwanth quietly waited.

After a brief conversation, Siddu returned.

There was genuine regret in his eyes.

"Yash..."

"I'm really sorry."

"I have to leave immediately."

"It's an important appointment."

Yashwanth's face instantly fell.

"But..."

"We were going to..."

He couldn't finish the sentence.

The words died in his throat.

For a brief moment, disappointment filled his heart.

Then he looked at Siddu.

He remembered that Siddu had flown all the way from France just because he was worried about him.

He was already carrying responsibilities far greater than his own.

How could he ask him to stay?

Yashwanth forced a smile.

"It's okay."

"I'll handle it."

Siddu looked at him apologetically.

"I'm sorry, Yash."

"If I had a choice..."

"I would never leave you alone today."

Yashwanth smiled weakly.

"I know."

The two friends exchanged one final look.

Without another word...

Siddu stepped into a waiting cab.

As the vehicle slowly disappeared down the road...

Yashwanth stood there, watching until it vanished from sight.

A strange emptiness settled inside him.

"First Varsha..."

"And now even Siddu has gone..."

For a moment...

It felt as though every person who gave him strength was slowly moving away from him.

But then...

Siddu's words echoed inside his mind.

"Speak the truth."

Taking a deep breath...

He gathered every ounce of courage left within him.

Step by step...

He walked toward his parents' house.

Finally...

He stood before the familiar front door.

His trembling hand reached for the doorbell.

Ding... Dong...

A few seconds later...

The door slowly opened.

Standing there...

Was his father.

The moment he saw Yashwanth...

His face lit up with joy.

"Yash!"

Without a second thought...

He pulled his son into a warm embrace.

"My boy..."

"You came without even telling us!"

Yashwanth stood motionless in his father's arms.

The warmth of that embrace only made the storm inside him stronger.

How could he wipe away the smile on his father's face?

How could he tell him that he couldn't accept the marriage they had arranged?

Yet...

How could he betray the woman who had entrusted him with her heart?

His father's dreams...

Or Varsha's love.

Standing at the doorstep...

Yashwanth found himself caught between the two.

And for the first time that day...

Without Siddu standing beside him...

He truly realized...

That this battle was his to fight alone.
